conventions.offline_first: Local storage writes before HTTP — same pattern as AnswerOutboxDao
conventions.dependency_injection: GetIt lazy singletons via module functions
conventions.drift_migrations: Additive schema migrations only — no data loss
conventions.equatable_models: ViolationEvent extends Equatable for test assertions

findings.title: Drift generated files (*.g.dart) are not committed — build_runner required
findings.description: LocalViolationDao and LocalViolationsTable use the @DriftAccessor and @DataClassName annotations. The generated *.g.dart files (created by build_runner) are not present in the repo. Running the app without first running 'dart run build_runner build' will fail with a missing import error.
findings.required_action: Document the build_runner requirement clearly in the release notes. Add *.g.dart to .gitignore if not already present.
findings.resolution: Documented in phase release notes as a required pre-build step. The 'dart run build_runner build --delete-conflicting-outputs' command is listed in the verification gate section.
references: Drift documentation: build_runner required for code generation

findings.title: security_module.dart imports security_module.dart via getIt singleton chain
findings.description: The module file imports LockdownService which imports ViolationReporter which imports LocalViolationDao which imports AppDatabase which is constructed with the DAOs. This forms a standard lazy-singleton DI chain with no circular references.
findings.required_action: No circular dependency found. The DI chain is linear: security_module → ViolationReporter → LocalViolationDao → AppDatabase. This is correct DI behavior.
findings.resolution: Not a defect — standard lazy DI. No changes needed.

findings.title: ViolationReporter retries all unsent rows on every retryUnsent call — no batch limit
findings.description: If 500 violations are unsent, retryUnsent will attempt to POST all 500 in sequence. A single failure stops the loop, but there is no per-call batch cap. Under severe network degradation, this could cause long-running retry loops.
findings.evidence: for (final row in unsent) { ... try await _apiClient.post(...); ... }
findings.required_action: ADVISORY: Consider adding a per-call batch limit (e.g., max 50 rows per retryUnsent call) with a resume cursor. Current approach is acceptable for MVP where violation volume is bounded by session length.
findings.resolution: ADVISORY: Accepted as-is for MVP. The retry loop stops on the first failure, so under normal network conditions it completes quickly. The batch limit improvement is documented as a post-MVP optimization.

findings.title: ForbiddenAppsConfig.load() throws on malformed JSON — no graceful degradation
findings.description: If the bundled forbidden_apps.json is corrupted, ForbiddenAppsConfig.load() rethrows the FormatException. The service's initialize() catches this and rethrows, crashing the app at startup. A corrupted config file would prevent the entire app from launching.
findings.evidence: throw const FormatException('forbidden_apps.json must be an object with windows/macos arrays')
findings.required_action: ADVISORY: Consider falling back to an empty config (no forbidden apps = no enforcement) if the asset fails to parse. Current behavior is acceptable if the file is treated as infrastructure (must be correct).
findings.resolution: ADVISORY: Accepted as-is. The forbidden_apps.json is a deployment artifact managed alongside the app binary. A corrupt config file indicates a broken deployment, not a runtime failure mode. Logging in initialize() surfaces the error clearly.

findings.title: Tests require mocktail and bloc_test — verify pubspec.yaml dependencies
findings.description: The test files use mocktail (Mock classes) and bloc_test (blocTest). These packages must be in dev_dependencies in pubspec.yaml. The existing test suite uses these packages, so they are likely already present, but this was not verified.
findings.required_action: Verify that mocktail and bloc_test are declared in pubspec.yaml dev_dependencies before merging.

findings.title: Verification gates (build, test, analyze) could not run — toolchain unavailable
findings.description: Flutter, Dart, CMake, and MSVC are not present in PATH. The native C++ compilation, Dart code generation (build_runner), flutter analyze, and flutter test could not be executed. All findings above are from static review only.
findings.required_action: Gate commands must be run manually in a Windows environment with the full Flutter toolchain installed.

verdict_reason: 2 HIGH findings are resolved (build_runner step documented, no circular DI). 2 MEDIUM advisories accepted as-is for MVP (batch retry limit, asset-on-disk contract). 2 NOTED findings (test deps, toolchain) require manual verification. Phase 04 code is structurally sound.
